title: Action de Galois sur Teichmüller : notes manuscrites (s.d.).

deep.reconstruction:
Context: on the previous page Grothendieck takes K a number field and X a smooth, geometrically connected quasi-projective K-variety. I is a finite set of K-rational points of X, and Π1(X,I) is the fundamental groupoid with base-point set I. He asks how Π1(X,I) relates to π1(U_{0,3}), where U_{0,3} = P^1 − {0,1,∞}, from the point of view of the Γ-action (Γ = Gal(K̄/K)). He proposes to combine Lefschetz-type theorems with Belyi's theorem to obtain K-morphisms (44): I ⊂ C →i X and f: C → U_{0,3}. Here C is a curve through I, i is surjective on (geometric) fundamental groups, and f is finite étale; f is Belyi's map with the fibre over {0,1,∞} removed.

This page draws the consequences.
(1) Since i_* is surjective, Π1(X,I) is a quotient of Π1(C,I). The same holds for the profinite completions: Π̂1(X,I) is a quotient of Π̂1(C,I).
(2) Π1(C,I) is a 'finite covering' of Π1(U_{0,3},·). He corrects this ('plus correctement'): let I_0 = f(I), a finite set of K-points of U_{0,3}, and I' = f^{-1}f(I) = f^{-1}(I_0) the saturation of I. Then:
- Π1(C;I) is a full subgroupoid of Π1(C;I'). The page writes U_{0,3}, a slip.
- Π1(C;I') is a finite covering of the groupoid Π1(U_{0,3};I_0): a faithful functor coming from a finite étale cover, i.e. an open-index subgroupoid.
- The same holds for the profinite completions.
(3) Hence the Γ-action on Π̂1(X) is known once one knows the action on Π̂1(C,I'). That groupoid is a finite covering of Π̂1(U_{0,3};I_0), so it should be determined by the Γ-action on Π̂1(U_{0,3};I_0). A crossed-out sentence starts to say this.

The next page completes the argument:
- For x,y in C the map Hom_{Π̂1(C)}(x,y) → Hom_{Π̂1(U_{0,3})}(fx,fy) is injective, so the action upstairs is the restriction of the action downstairs.
- The saturation I' need not consist of K-rational points, so Γ permutes the base points (a twisted, descent-type action). Still, knowing the Γ-action on Π̂1(U_{0,3};I_0) implies knowing it on Π̂1(X,I).

In modern terms: by Lefschetz + Belyi, the outer/groupoid Galois action on the étale fundamental groupoid of any smooth geometrically connected variety over a number field, with rational base points, is a subquotient of the Galois action on the profinite fundamental groupoid of P^1 − {0,1,∞} with finitely many K-rational base points. This makes the tripod U_{0,3} 'universal' for Galois actions on fundamental groupoids, in the base-point-groupoid formulation that Grothendieck favours in the Esquisse.
errors: Slip: 'Π1(U_{0,3};I) est un sous-groupoïde plein de Π1(U_{0,3};I')' should read Π1(C;I) ⊂ Π1(C;I'). Here I and I' are subsets of C, not of U_{0,3}.

Gap: one must ensure f(I) ⊂ U_{0,3}, i.e. no point of I is sent by the Belyi map to 0, 1 or ∞, so that I lies in the open curve C on which f is étale. Belyi's construction does not automatically guarantee this. It needs an extra argument (a Belyi map 'non-critical'/avoiding the cusps at prescribed points), not addressed on the page.

Gap: the existence of a curve C through the prescribed finite set I with π1(C_{K̄}) → π1(X_{K̄}) surjective, for X merely quasi-projective, is asserted only as 'doit pouvoir' (Lefschetz-type theorems for quasi-projective varieties through given points). It is plausible but not proved here.

Caution: I' = f^{-1}(I_0) generally contains non-K-rational points, so Γ acts on Π̂1(C;I') while permuting objects. Grothendieck himself flags this on the next page; the phrase 'opération de Γ' must be read as an action with a Γ-set of base points.

ideas.what: Reduce Galois action on π1 of an arbitrary smooth variety over a number field to that on a curve via a Lefschetz curve section C ⊂ X with π1-surjection passing through given base points.
ideas.modern_name: Lefschetz-type theorem for fundamental groups (curve sections), with base points
ideas.usually_credited_to: Lefschetz; Grothendieck SGA2 for étale π1 (projective case); Goresky–MacPherson, Hamm–Lê for quasi-projective
ideas.where_published: SGA 2 (Lefschetz theorems for π1); the quasi-projective version through given points is not in his published texts as far as I know

ideas.what: Use a Belyi map f: C → P^1 − {0,1,∞}, finite étale on the open curve C, to realize Π1(C;I') as a finite covering (open subgroupoid) of Π1(U_{0,3};I_0) with I_0 = f(I) rational points.
ideas.modern_name: Belyi's theorem applied to fundamental groupoids / open subgroupoids
ideas.usually_credited_to: Belyi (1979); faithfulness consequence discussed by Grothendieck (Esquisse), Ihara, Deligne
ideas.where_published: Esquisse d'un programme (1984), Belyi's theorem and faithfulness of Γ on π̂1(P^1−3 pts); the groupoid/several-base-point reduction for arbitrary X is not stated there in this form

ideas.what: Conclusion: the Γ-action on Π̂1(X,I) for any smooth geometrically connected quasi-projective X/K is determined (as a subquotient) by the Γ-action on the profinite fundamental groupoid Π̂1(U_{0,3};I_0) with finitely many K-rational base points. It passes through the saturation I' = f^{-1}f(I), on which Γ acts by permutation.
ideas.modern_name: Universality of the tripod for Galois actions on fundamental groupoids; cf. 'Belyi cuspidalization' style arguments
ideas.usually_credited_to: Folklore after Belyi/Grothendieck; related techniques in Mochizuki's absolute anabelian geometry (Belyi cuspidalization, noncritical Belyi maps, ~2003–2007)
ideas.where_published: Spirit present in Esquisse d'un programme; explicit groupoid statement not known to me in published texts

ideas.what: Full subgroupoid on I inside the groupoid on the saturated set I', and injectivity of Hom-sets under a finite étale map (next page). This lets the action upstairs be recovered by restriction.
ideas.modern_name: Fundamental groupoid of a finite étale cover as open subgroupoid; base change of base-point sets
ideas.usually_credited_to: Standard (SGA1 Galois theory; Brown for groupoids with many base points)
ideas.where_published: SGA 1 (Galois theory of finite étale covers); groupoid language in Esquisse

missed.claim: Grothendieck reduces Galois action on fundamental groupoids of arbitrary varieties with rational base points to the tripod with rational base points via Lefschetz + Belyi. This needs Belyi maps sending prescribed points into U_{0,3} (not to cusps). That is exactly the issue later addressed by Mochizuki's 'noncritical Belyi maps' and 'Belyi cuspidalization' in absolute anabelian geometry. The page shows Grothendieck already used the Belyi map as a device to transport rational points/base points (hence decomposition-type data) to P^1−{0,1,∞}.
missed.quote: prenons la saturée I'=f^{-1}f(I)=f^{-1}(I_0) de I, ... Ainsi, l'opération de Γ sur \hat Π_1(X) est connue quand on connaît l'opération sur \hat Π_1(C,\tilde I), qui est un rev. fini de \hat Π_1(U_{0,3};I_0)
missed.why_it_might_matter_today: A historical precursor for Belyi-type cuspidalization arguments. It is also a precise formulation, with groupoids on several rational base points, of why GT-type information on the tripod controls Galois actions on all π1's, including the gap concerning points falling on cusps.

missed.quote: on doit pouvoir trouver des homomorphismes de schémas sur K  I ⊂ C → X, f : C → U_{0,3}  (44)
missed.why_it_might_matter_today: Both are now provable with known tools (Goresky–MacPherson-type Lefschetz plus Bertini through points; noncritical Belyi maps). Together they give the precise statement, which is not commonly stated in exactly this groupoid form.

deep.surprise_reason: The reduction via Belyi to the tripod is the well-known rationale of the Esquisse. The groupoid-with-rational-base-points version for arbitrary quasi-projective X via Lefschetz is a nice unpublished detail. It anticipates issues treated later in Mochizuki's Belyi cuspidalization, but it is largely folklore-level.

Line 3: 'Π1(C,I)': the C is written over a struck/blotted X.
Line 4: '[?] de Π̂1(C,I)' is 'quotient de Π̂1(C,I)'.
Line 6: 'comme un sous-groupe[?] fini de Π1(U_{0,3},I)' is most likely 'comme un revêtement fini de Π1(U_{0,3},I)'.
'=g^{-1}(I_0)' is '=f^{-1}(I_0)', with f written over an erasure.
'qui lui est un rev. fini du groupoïde de Π1(U_{0,3};I_0)' is probably 'rev. fini du groupoïde Π1(U_{0,3};I_0)'.
'Π̂1(C,Ĩ)': the tilde-I there denotes the saturation I'.
The struck final line begins roughly 'on en déduit son action sur Π̂1(C,I')...'; it is not about Π̂1(U_{0,3}).
'l'opération de Γ sur Π̂1(X)' is correct; the image shows Π̂1(X) without base points there.
